name: White Desert (by Malvah)
awwwardsEvidence: WebSearch only (awwwards.com unreachable from this environment, DNS failure in WebFetch and Playwright). Query `"White Desert" Antarctica website awwwards "Site of the Day" studio credits` returned the result titled 'White Desert - Awwwards SOTD' (awwwards.com/sites/white-desert) with snippet 'Site of the Day - Sep 11, 2026' and credits 'Malvah ^PRO, Geoff Dawes, Usudo'; an LBB Online interview ('Getting to Know… Malvah Studio') describes Malvah's work for White Desert. Award page itself not loaded.

observed.layout: ≈20 800 px desktop document. Hero = muted autoplay film (no poster: grey frame until it plays) with 'ANTARCTICA' set across the bottom; uppercase serif statement on white with faint vertical grid lines (fixed '.grid-overlay'); 'OUR TRIPS' cards; 'OUR CAMPS' title over a sticky aerial ice photo while camp cards slide sideways (sticky '.horizontal-scroll_wrapper'); 'mist' transitions between scenes (sticky '.mist-transition_image-container'); a dark flight panel with numbers (FLYING TIME 05:30 HRS, 4,220 KM / 2,610 MI, -5°C / 23°F) beside a map of the route; a giant route code 'CPT – WFR'; footer with a full-width 'WHITE DESERT' wordmark.
observed.typography: Computed: h1 'Antarctica' Oswald 400, 256 px, line-height 256 px, uppercase (80 px on 390 mobile); 'CPT – WFR' Oswald 320 px (200 px mobile); h2/statement in 'Cardinal Classic Long' (serif) 90 px uppercase; paragraphs Cardinal Classic Long 18 px; UI in Inter Tight 500. Three families: condensed sans for monuments, serif for voice, grotesk for UI.
observed.imagery: Full-bleed aerial and ground photography of ice, blue ice runways, camps; colour stays within white/ice-blue with one orange accent (the vertical 'Rates' tab, the 'Enquire' pill on mobile).
observed.motion: Lenis smooth scroll (html.lenis); sticky horizontal camp rail and sticky mist dissolves seen across sequential wheel screenshots; custom cursor element. Reduced-motion emulation produced the same screenshots: no visible change.
observed.responsive: Mobile keeps the chapters, condenses type (h1 80 px), 'Menu' + 'Enquire' pill top bar. A chat prompt + cookie banner covered the bottom ≈35% of every mobile screenshot.

whyItWorks: Facts are the spectacle: the flight panel turns hours, distance and temperature into a scene, and one condensed typeface at 256–320 px carries the place name and the route code like signage. One orange accent on a neutral palette is enough to mark every action.
principles: Set the one number that defines the experience (flight time, smoking time) huge, as a scene of its own.
Use a condensed display face at monument size for the place name or code; keep body text in another voice.
One saturated accent on a neutral palette, reserved for actions and the key number.
Let a sticky full-bleed photo hold still while information changes over it.
doNotCarryOver: Hero film without a poster (grey first frame) and no reduced-motion alternative.
Focus outline at 0 px on most nav buttons (Tab showed outline=auto 0px).
Chat prompt and cookie banner stacked over the mobile first screen.
Lenis smooth scroll (we keep native scroll).
Their Oswald/Cardinal pairing, ice palette, wordmark and photos.

name: Gourou Indian Food Company (design 13g, dev Thomas Carré)
awwwardsEvidence: WebSearch only: the result 'Gourou Indian Food - Awwwards Honorable Mention' (awwwards.com/sites/gourou-indian-food) and Thomas Carré's Awwwards profile snippet 'Gourou Indian Food WEBSITE HM Honorable Mention Feb 17, 2026'. The live footer credits 'Design : 13g.fr' and 'Dev : Thomas Carré', which matches the award credit. Award page not loaded (awwwards.com unreachable).

observed.layout: ≈8 500 px desktop, ≈10 300 px mobile. Header: logo, 'Réserver' and 'Emporter' outlined pills, red 'Recrutement'. Hero: two photos side by side (kitchen + dish) and 'INDIAN FOOD COMPANY' set edge to edge in blue; a 'TO PARIS' marquee with a delivery-truck drawing; red full-width bands; a menu grid where every dish is a saturated card (yellow/blue/green/red/orange) with the Hindi name, the French/English name and a one-line description; 'SHOP' merch section; a closing block with address, metro line, hours and phone, then a blue footer nav.
observed.typography: Computed: Poppins 700 uppercase everywhere (h2 86.4 px 'INDIAN FOOD COMPANY', section titles 28.8 px, body 14.4 px), Oswald loaded; Devanagari script used as a second graphic voice beside each dish.
observed.imagery: Dish cut-outs on flat colour cards, candid kitchen photos of staff in branded T-shirts, a top-down table shot; four autoplay videos (muted).
observed.motion: GSAP + Lenis present; marquees, page loader and transition overlays (fixed .loader / .transition), Lottie hover videos. Reduced-motion emulation looked the same as normal.
observed.responsive: Mobile stacks the cards one per row, keeps the colour blocks, 'Recrutement' + burger in the header. Phone link is tel:0140563595 (valid).

whyItWorks: The menu is the hero: each dish gets its own card in the brand palette, with two scripts and a plain description, so browsing the menu feels like part of the identity instead of a PDF. Practical facts (address, metro, hours, phone) are written out in one block at the end.
principles: Make the menu itself the signature component, styled in the brand system.
Give each dish its real name and one plain line; no adjectives needed.
End with address, transit, hours and phone together in one readable block.
Keep reserve/takeaway actions in the header from the first frame.
doNotCarryOver: Body copy at 14.4 px with 15.8 px line-height in places (too tight).
No change at all under prefers-reduced-motion (marquees, loader).
Five saturated colours at once (works for their brand, not for a monochrome direction).
Their logo, palette, Devanagari treatment and photos.
